un.name: United Nations
descriptions: Founded in 1945 after the Second World War
Has 193 member states, nearly every country in the world
Has 6 official languages: English, French, Spanish, Russian, Chinese and Arabic
Oversees the WHO, UNICEF, UNESCO and UNHCR
Its New York headquarters sits on international territory

eu.name: European Union
descriptions: Created in 1993 with the Treaty of Maastricht
Brings together 27 European countries with around 450 million inhabitants
The euro is its common currency, used in 21 countries
Received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2012
Its blue flag bears 12 golden stars in a circle

nato.name: NATO
descriptions: Military alliance created in 1949 after the Second World War
Has 32 member countries, including the United States and France
Its principle: an attack on one member is an attack on all
Has a futuristic Brussels headquarters inaugurated in 2017
Its full name is North Atlantic Treaty Organization

african-union.name: African Union
descriptions: Created in 2002 to replace the Organisation of African Unity
Has 55 member states, all African countries
Its headquarters was built in Ethiopia with China's help
Has its own peacekeeping force to intervene on the continent
Aspires to a single African currency in the future

arab-league.name: Arab League
descriptions: Founded in 1945, it is one of the oldest regional organizations
Has 22 member countries, from Morocco to Iraq
Its headquarters has been in Cairo, Egypt since its creation
Its green flag symbolizes Islam, the majority religion of its members
Represents nearly 450 million Arabic speakers

asean.name: ASEAN
descriptions: Association of Southeast Asian Nations, founded in 1967
Brings together 11 countries such as Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia
Represents 670 million inhabitants
Has its own annual summit of heads of state
Aims for a free trade zone among its members

g7.name: G7
descriptions: Group of the 7 major developed economies in the world
Brings together USA, Canada, UK, France, Germany, Italy and Japan
Created in 1975 after the oil shock
The annual summit changes host country every year
Russia was part of it from 1998 to 2014, forming the G8

g20.name: G20
descriptions: Group of the 20 largest economies in the world
Includes China, India, Brazil and South Africa in addition to the G7
Represents 85% of the world economy
First summit in 2008 during the financial crisis
The presidency rotates among member countries each year

interpol.name: Interpol
descriptions: Largest police organization in the world, created in 1923
Has 196 member countries linked by databases
Its world headquarters is in Lyon, France
Issues red notices to track fugitive criminals
Does not make arrests itself, it coordinates police forces

wto.name: World Trade Organization
descriptions: Created in 1995 to regulate trade between countries
Has 166 member countries representing 98% of world trade
Its headquarters is in a former villa on the shore of Lake Geneva
Settles trade disputes between nations
Its decisions can impose fines on countries

opec.name: OPEC
descriptions: Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries, founded in 1960
Has 12 member countries like Saudi Arabia and Venezuela
Controls about 40% of world oil production
Decides together on the quantities of oil to produce
Can drive global oil prices up or down

imf.name: International Monetary Fund
descriptions: Created in 1944 to stabilize the world economy
Has 190 member countries that contribute to its common fund
Lends money to countries in financial difficulty
Its headquarters is in Washington, right next to the White House
Also holds gold reserves to back its loans

world-bank.name: World Bank
descriptions: Founded in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference
Helps poor countries with loans for development
Funds schools, roads and hospitals in over 100 countries
Has 189 member countries
Its official goal: eliminate extreme poverty by 2030

oecd.name: OECD
descriptions: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, created in 1961
Brings together 38 of the world's most developed countries
Its headquarters is at the Château de la Muette in Paris
Publishes the famous PISA ranking of school systems
Nicknamed the club of rich countries

brics.name: BRICS
descriptions: Group formed by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa
Created in 2009 to counterbalance Western countries
Represents over 40% of the world's population
Iran, Egypt and the UAE joined them in 2024
Has its own bank to finance its projects

mercosur.name: Mercosur
descriptions: Common market of South America, created in 1991
Has 5 members: Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia
Its headquarters is in the Uruguayan capital, Montevideo
Allows free movement of goods between members
Represents over 290 million inhabitants

usmca.name: USMCA
descriptions: Free trade agreement between USA, Mexico and Canada
Entered into force in 2020, replacing the former NAFTA
Affects nearly 500 million people
The agreement is renegotiated every 6 years between the 3 countries
Represents one of the world's largest trade zones

ecb.name: European Central Bank
descriptions: Created in 1998 to manage the euro, the European currency
Its headquarters is a 185 m glass tower in Frankfurt
Sets interest rates in the eurozone
Prints euro banknotes used by 350 million people
Its leaders meet every 6 weeks

iaea.name: IAEA
descriptions: International Atomic Energy Agency, founded in 1957
Monitors civilian and military nuclear use around the world
Has 178 member states
Its headquarters is in Vienna, at the UN international center
Received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2005

fifa.name: FIFA
descriptions: International Federation of Football, founded in Paris in 1904
Has 211 national federations, more than the UN
Organizes the World Cup every 4 years since 1930
Its headquarters has been in Zurich, Switzerland since 1932
The 1998 World Cup in France drew 1.3 billion viewers

uefa.name: UEFA
descriptions: Union of European Football Associations, created in 1954
Organizes the Champions League and the Euro every 4 years
Has 55 member federations
Its headquarters is on the shore of Lake Geneva, in Nyon, Switzerland
The Champions League is the most-watched club competition in the world

ioc.name: International Olympic Committee
descriptions: Founded by Pierre de Coubertin in 1894
Organizes the Summer and Winter Olympic Games every 2 years alternately
Its headquarters is in Lausanne, the Olympic capital
Chooses the host city for the Games 7 years in advance
The Olympic flag with 5 rings symbolizes the 5 continents

world-rugby.name: World Rugby
descriptions: Governing body of world rugby, created in 1886
Has 132 national federations
Organizes the Rugby World Cup every 4 years
Its headquarters is in Dublin, Ireland
The World Cup trophy is called the Webb Ellis Cup

fiba.name: FIBA
descriptions: International Basketball Federation, founded in 1932
Has 213 member federations worldwide
Its headquarters is in Mies, near Geneva
Organizes the Basketball World Cup every 4 years
Basketball is the second most practiced sport in the world

caf.name: Confederation of African Football
descriptions: Founded in 1957 during a meeting in Khartoum
Has 54 member federations
Organizes the Africa Cup of Nations every 2 years
Its headquarters has been in Egypt since its creation
Egypt has won the AFCON 7 times, a continental record

conmebol.name: CONMEBOL
descriptions: Oldest football confederation, created in 1916
Brings together 10 South American countries
Organizes the Copa America, the oldest continental competition
Its headquarters is in Luque, near Asunción in Paraguay
Argentina and Uruguay have won the most Copa America titles

afc.name: Asian Football Confederation
descriptions: Asian football confederation, created in 1954
Has 47 national federations
Organizes the Asian Cup of Nations every 4 years
Its headquarters is in Malaysia, in Kuala Lumpur
Japan has won the Asian Cup 4 times, a record

fia.name: FIA
descriptions: International Automobile Federation, created in 1904
Governs Formula 1, rally racing and 245 million motorists
Its headquarters is at Place de la Concorde in Paris
Decides the technical rules for racing cars
The F1 World Championship has existed since 1950

itf.name: International Tennis Federation
descriptions: Founded in Paris in 1913, then moved to London
Has 213 national federations
Organizes the Davis Cup and the Billie Jean King Cup
Oversees the 4 Grand Slam tournaments
Tennis became a permanent Olympic sport in 1988

red-cross.name: International Red Cross
descriptions: Founded in 1863 by the Swiss Henry Dunant
Has received the Nobel Peace Prize 3 times
Its emblem, a red cross on a white background, is the reverse of the Swiss flag
Operates in wars and natural disasters
Has 192 national societies around the world

msf.name: Doctors Without Borders
descriptions: Created in Paris in 1971 by French doctors
Sends doctors to war zones and disaster areas
Received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1999
Operates in over 70 countries each year
Funded 97% by private donations to remain independent

unicef.name: UNICEF
descriptions: United Nations Children's Fund, created in 1946
Present in 190 countries to help children
Vaccinates nearly half the world's children every year
Its headquarters is in New York, in the heart of Manhattan
Its former logo featured a mother and child

who.name: World Health Organization
descriptions: Created in 1948, it is the UN's health agency
Has 194 member states
Eradicated smallpox from the planet in 1980
Coordinates the fight against epidemics like COVID-19
Its emblem is a staff with a coiled snake, a medical symbol

amnesty.name: Amnesty International
descriptions: NGO founded in London in 1961 by a British lawyer
Defends human rights around the world
Received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977
Has 10 million members and supporters
Its logo features a candle surrounded by barbed wire

greenpeace.name: Greenpeace
descriptions: Environmental NGO founded in 1971 in Canada
Present in 55 countries with 3 million members
Its ship Rainbow Warrior was sunk in 1985
Fights pollution, nuclear power and deforestation
Refuses donations from governments and companies to stay free

wwf.name: WWF
descriptions: Nature foundation created in 1961 in Switzerland
Its logo features a panda drawn in 1961
Works in 100 countries to protect nature
Its headquarters is in Gland, on the shore of Lake Geneva
World's largest environmental organization by size

oxfam.name: Oxfam
descriptions: Confederation of 21 NGOs founded in Oxford in 1942
Helps fight poverty in over 90 countries
Its international headquarters is in Nairobi, Kenya
Publishes an annual report on global inequalities
Also runs a large network of charity shops in Europe

care.name: CARE International
descriptions: NGO created in 1945 to send food parcels to post-war Europe
Present in over 100 countries today
Helps 170 million people every year
Focuses on aid to women and girls
Its name CARE originally meant Cooperative for American Remittances to Europe

save-children.name: Save the Children
descriptions: Founded in 1919 in London to help European children after the First World War
Its founder Eglantyne Jebb wrote the first rights of the child
Present in over 100 countries
Helps about 45 million children every year
Its logo features a child held by protective arms
